## Why Candidate Experience Is a Business Priority

A poor candidate experience can hurt an employer in several ways. Candidates who have a negative experience may:

- Tell others about it
- Leave negative reviews on employer review sites
- Decline to apply again
- Stop using your product or service, if they are also customers

We quote no figures for how often this happens, because we have not cited a source. Use the checklist to find your own gaps.

### The 50-Point Audit Checklist

The thresholds below are suggestions, not benchmarks. Adjust them to your market and roles.

#### Job Discovery (Points 1-10)

- ☐ Career page loads quickly
- ☐ Jobs are searchable by location, function and level
- ☐ Each posting includes a salary range
- ☐ Company culture is shown with authentic content
- ☐ Benefits are listed clearly
- ☐ The application process timeline is visible
- ☐ Mobile-optimized experience
- ☐ Job descriptions use inclusive language
- ☐ Clear value proposition for candidates
- ☐ Easy-to-find "Apply" button

#### Application Process (Points 11-20)

- ☐ Application is short enough to finish in one sitting
- ☐ Resume parsing works accurately
- ☐ No duplicate data entry required
- ☐ Quick-apply options enabled where useful
- ☐ Progress indicator shows completion status
- ☐ Save and resume functionality
- ☐ Account creation not required to apply
- ☐ Confirmation email sent immediately
- ☐ Expected timeline communicated
- ☐ Accessibility standards met (for example WCAG)

#### Screening Phase (Points 21-30)

- ☐ Prompt response after application
- ☐ Personalized rejection emails, not generic ones
- ☐ Phone screen scheduled promptly
- ☐ Interviewer is prepared (has reviewed the resume)
- ☐ Candidate receives the agenda before the screen
- ☐ Two-way conversation, not an interrogation
- ☐ Next steps communicated clearly
- ☐ Timeline commitments honored
- ☐ Candidate can ask questions
- ☐ Feedback provided to unsuccessful candidates

#### Interview Stage (Points 31-40)

- ☐ Self-service scheduling available
- ☐ Interview preparation guide sent in advance
- ☐ Interviewers introduce themselves and their role
- ☐ Questions are relevant and non-discriminatory
- ☐ Candidate meets future teammates
- ☐ Office tour or virtual workspace demo
- ☐ A reasonable number of rounds
- ☐ Travel reimbursement offered if applicable
- ☐ Accommodations offered proactively
- ☐ Decision communicated promptly

#### Offer and Close (Points 41-50)

- ☐ Verbal offer followed by a written one
- ☐ Offer details are comprehensive and clear
- ☐ Reasonable decision timeline
- ☐ Negotiation handled professionally
- ☐ Rejection calls for finalists, not email
- ☐ Pre-boarding communication begins immediately
- ☐ Welcome materials sent before day one
- ☐ First-day logistics clearly communicated
- ☐ Candidate experience survey sent
- ☐ Feedback loop to improve the process

### Scoring Your Audit

Count the boxes you can tick and compare your result over time. As a rough self-assessment, not a benchmark:

- Most boxes ticked: a strong experience, so keep it under review
- About half ticked: good in places with clear room for improvement
- Fewer than half ticked: gaps likely affecting candidates, so redesign the weakest stages first

### Quick Wins

If you have many gaps, start with these:

- Shorten the application
- Send an acknowledgement straight away
- Respond to every candidate
- Give feedback to interviewed candidates
